tasks.title: The shared path-boundary helper
tasks.objective: Add assert_target_destination(target, dst) to scaffold.py: resolve target once, resolve dst strict=False, reject symlink loops and any resolved path outside the resolved target, return dst for chaining. Reimplement check_record_origin_writable on it, closing its missing-tail-below-symlinked-ancestor gap. Add the helper's unit tests. (The cross-module structural anti-reopen scan is Task 4's deliverable, once all three commands are migrated.)
acceptance_criteria: assert_target_destination refuses a destination whose path resolves outside the resolved target root, whether reached via a symlinked destination, a symlinked ancestor above the target, a `..` traversal, a symlink loop, OR a symlink inside the target that points outside it; it returns the destination unchanged for a legal in-boundary path.

It resolves the tail with strict=False so a not-yet-existing destination below a symlinked ancestor is still refused; check_record_origin_writable is reimplemented on top of it and no longer misses that case.
Every existing test that exercises check_record_origin_writable stays green with no weakening.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "assert_target_destination or origin_writable or boundary_helper or path_boundary"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That the helper resolves with strict=False and refuses an in-target symlink that points outside (not special-cased), and that reimplementing check_record_origin_writable did not change behaviour for any legal path an existing caller relies on. (The structural anti-reopen scan is Task 4's deliverable — do not expect it here.)

tasks.title: init routes every write site through the boundary helper
tasks.objective: Route every init filesystem write, mkdir, delete and copy destination through assert_target_destination, hoisted into a preflight before the first mutation so an escape stops init clean rather than mid-write. Validate copytree/rmtree roots before the walk and preflight the dirs_exist_ok merge leaves; tree copies preserve source symlinks (symlinks=True) rather than follow them. Add per-site escape tests; every existing init test stays green unweakened.
acceptance_criteria: Every init write site routes its destination through assert_target_destination, and the checks run in a preflight before the first mutation so a refused escape leaves the target unmodified (no partial write).
Each init copytree/rmtree validates its root destination before the walk/delete, and the dirs_exist_ok merge destinations are each preflighted.
A test asserts init refuses a symlinked destination and a symlinked ancestor and leaves the target clean; a legal init produces the same result as before.
Every existing init test stays green with no test weakened.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "init"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That the check is a PREFLIGHT before the first mutation (AC2 in the plan) — an escape must stop init before any file is written, not part-way — and that no init write site bypasses the helper. That no existing init behaviour test was weakened to pass.

The checks run in a preflight before the first mutation, so a refused escape leaves the target unmodified.

verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "adopt"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That vendor_file's local check is genuinely REPLACED by the shared helper (not left alongside it), that all ~18 previously-unguarded adopt sites now route through it, and the preflight fires before the first mutation. That no existing adopt behaviour test was weakened.

tasks.title: upgrade routes every write site through the boundary helper
tasks.objective: Route every upgrade write site through assert_target_destination: copytree/rmtree roots validated before the walk, the ~15 direct writes, and the two partial checks (.agents root, harness.yaml leaf) routed through the helper while keeping their legacy-content validation. Tree copies preserve source symlinks. Add per-site escape tests. Now that all three commands route through the helper, add the structural anti-reopen scan (AC4). Existing upgrade tests stay green.
acceptance_criteria: Every upgrade write site routes its destination through assert_target_destination; the copytree/rmtree roots are validated before the walk/delete and the two partial checks route through the helper while retaining their legacy-content validation.
The checks run in a preflight before the first mutation, so a refused escape leaves the target unmodified.
A test asserts upgrade refuses a symlinked destination and a symlinked ancestor and leaves the target clean; a legal upgrade produces the same result as before.

A structural test reads the scaffold.py (init), adopt.py and upgrade.py modules and fails if any raw filesystem-mutating call (shutil.copy*/move/copytree/rmtree, os.mkdir/makedirs/remove/rmdir/rename/symlink, Path.write_text/write_bytes, open(...,'w'|'a'|'x')) appears outside the shared boundary helper — so a FUTURE unguarded site fails the suite, not just today's sites.
Every existing upgrade test stays green with no test weakened.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "upgrade or no_raw_write_primitive or anti_reopen"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That the copytree/rmtree replacement ROOTS are validated before the walk (a root check, not just leaf checks), that the two pre-existing partial checks now route through the shared helper without losing their legacy-content validation, and that the ~15 direct writes are all covered. CRUCIALLY: that the structural anti-reopen scan enumerates ALL THREE command modules and would FAIL if the helper were bypassed at any site — a scan that misses a module or a primitive is the durability hole this whole story exists to close. That no existing upgrade behaviour test was weakened.
